### Nifty Crashes 1,200 Points in 5-6 Trading Sessions (17,400 to 16,200) — April 29 – May 9, 2022
- **Source video:** #1004 — "1004 - Pre Market Report 09-May-2022.docx" (09 May 2022)
- **What happened:** On April 29, 2022 — the first trading session of the May series — Nifty was around 17,400. By May 9, SGX Nifty was indicating around 16,200, a straight cut of 1,200 points in just 5-6 trading sessions. The market was falling roughly 200-250 points every day. PR describes this as a period of intense, relentless selling pressure.
- **Market impact:** Indian equity markets in freefall; 1,200-point drop in under a week; daily losses of 200-250 points. Indian market described as 'really very bad' compared to US markets which were not as bad on close-to-close basis. SGX Nifty (global benchmark for India) signaling continued weakness.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** When a market falls 1,200 points in 5-6 sessions with daily 200-250 point drops, it reflects a systemic risk-off event, not a normal correction. Traders should note that such velocity of decline indicates panic and forced unwinding, and that waiting for stabilization before re-entering is prudent.
- **Verbatim quote:** "If you can remember on 29th April the first trading session of May series, Nifty was around 17,400. Now SGX Nifty indicating around 16,200. So that means it is a straight cut off 1,200 point in 5-6 trading sessions. So our market is falling almost 200 to 250 point every day."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### US Market Capitulation — Dow Plunges 750 Points, Nasdaq Down 27% Post-Fed Meeting, May 2022 — 9-10 May 2022
- **Source video:** #1006 — "1006 - Pre Market Report 10-May-2022.docx" (10 May 2022)
- **What happened:** Following the Federal Reserve's 50-basis-point rate hike on May 4, 2022, US equity markets entered a severe three-day selling phase. On the night of May 9, the Dow Jones was down approximately 400 points at the close of the Indian market, opened around -400, swung between -650 and -350 intraday, then collapsed 400 points in the final half hour from -350 to nearly -750 — a sharp late-session institutional sell-off. The Nasdaq had fallen 27% from its recent high, with 10% of that decline occurring in just the last three trading sessions, signaling complete capitulation by bulls. Tesla fell 11-12% separately on news of a production halt at its Shanghai factory due to China COVID lockdowns.
- **Market impact:** The last-half-hour 400-point Dow collapse represented institutional selling — professionals closing positions. The Nasdaq's 10% drop in three sessions indicated a capitulation-driven crash, not routine volatility. Sundar notes that in other countries futures margin is only 5-6%, so a 10% market fall triggers cascading margin calls and forced liquidation.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** A big fall toward the end of the day is a major cause for concern because amateurs/retail open the market while institutions/professionals close it — so late-session heavy selling signals institutional exit. In severe intense selling, by the time you realize what is happening, the game is over in three days. When the market falls 10%, individual stocks can fall 20-30%, and thin-margin futures positions get destroyed.
- **Verbatim quote:** "Then around 1230 midnight yesterday I just got up. I could not sleep. I was watching the Dow. And then in the last half an hour, Dow fell 400 point from minus 350 to minus 750 almost. Such a terrible fall in the last half an hour. And, you know, usually a bigger fall towards the end of the day is really a cause for concern. Why? Because I always say amateurs open the market and professionals close the market or retail people open the market, institutions close the market. So definitely that is an institutional selling."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### US April 2022 CPI Inflation Data Misses Expectations — 11 May 2022
- **Source video:** #1009 — "1009 - 16K Broken! Post Market Report 11-May-22.docx" (11 May 2022)
- **What happened:** The US released its April inflation (CPI) data: 8.3% versus the prior month's 8.5%, which was better sequentially, but worse than the market expectation of 8.1%. The moment the data was released, Dow futures fell nearly 400-500 points within minutes. The US 10-year bond yield spiked from 2.92% to 3.05%. Before the data, Dow futures were up 300+ points; after, they were down 200+, a 500-point swing. PR Sundar predicted the US market would fall at least 500 points when it opened, given the 800-point daily swings seen recently.
- **Market impact:** Global market sentiment flipped from positive to negative overnight. Indian market was expected to open lower and react negatively the next day (May 12, 2022). The data intensified fears of aggressive Fed rate hikes (0.5% or 0.75% speculation). This macro shock contributed to the ongoing market mayhem that PR Sundar had predicted for May.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Inflation data that improves month-on-month but misses expectations can still trigger sharp selloffs — the market focuses on the miss, not the improvement. The narrative battle (worst is over vs. higher than expected) drives the next day's direction. Fed rate decisions and inflation data are recurring volatility catalysts that will persist for many months.
- **Verbatim quote:** "The US inflation data came and it is better than the last month but worse than what was expected the moment the data came the Dow future fell nearly 400 500 points within few minutes and US 10-year bond yield shot up from 2.92 percent to 3.05 percent."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### Tulipomania - The 17th Century Tulip Bulb Bubble and Crash — 17th century (circa 1637)
- **Source video:** #0102 — "102 - What is VEGA in Options - Options Trading _ P R Sundar (Tamil).docx" (28 June 2020)
- **What happened:** In the 17th century, tulip bulbs in the European region (Netherlands) were normally white but became affected by a virus that changed their color, creating mixed-color tulips that people found very attractive. People went crazy over these colored tulips and prices started shooting up dramatically: from one dollar to two, five, ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand dollars. At the peak of the craziness, one tulip flower (Semper Augustus, meaning 'always the king' in Latin, named after Augustus Caesar) was traded for twelve acres of land, or approximately thirty-five thousand US dollars, equivalent to a skilled workman's ten-year salary. People disposed of all their properties to buy tulips at these peak prices. Then the market crashed. During that time, people used call options and put options to hedge their positions, though they were not aware of the formal names. The market was unregulated. This episode became known as Tulipomania.
- **Market impact:** A massive speculative bubble formed where tulip bulbs traded for extraordinary values (one flower for 12 acres of land or a worker's decade of salary). The subsequent crash wiped out wealth as people who had disposed of properties to buy tulips at peak prices lost everything. The event became a classic historical example of speculative mania and the greater fool theory.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** People buy without looking at intrinsic value — a tulip flower cannot be worth twenty thousand dollars in intrinsic value. People still buy because they think it can be sold for an even higher price later. This mentality is called Tulipomania, and in modern stock markets it is referred to as the 'greater fool theory' — a fool buys a share at a price much higher than intrinsic value expecting another greater fool to come and buy at a higher price so he can exit. The story illustrates the dangers of speculative bubbles where price detaches from fundamental value.
- **Verbatim quote:** "So people buy without looking at the intrinsic value. Now, one tulip flower cannot be twenty thousand dollars in its intrinsic value. Its real value is not that. People still buy because they think that it can be sold for twenty five thousand dollars or thirty thousand dollars later. So for this kind of mentality they have given a name called Tulipomania. You just go to Google type Tulipomania you will get all the details and in fact nowadays in stock market they use another name instead of Tulipomania they call it as a greater fool theory."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### Swiss National Bank hikes interest rates for first time in 15 years, triggering global panic — 16 Jun 2022
- **Source video:** #1071 — "1071 - 52 WEEK LOW BROKEN! Post Market Report 16-Jun-22.docx" (16 Jun 2022)
- **What happened:** News came during the Indian trading session that Switzerland had hiked interest rates — its first interest-rate hike in the last 15 years — and that another small European country also raised rates. - **Market impact:** European futures and Dow futures fell sharply; Nifty dropped more than 500 points from intraday high to intraday low; Bank Nifty fell more than 1000 points; the Metal index was down over 5%; brutal one-way selling with every minor 40-50 point bounce sold into. The sudden 11 a.m. reversal broke the prior swing low of 15,659 and yesterday's low, accelerating FII selling.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** FIIs use every gap-up to sell aggressively, especially on expiry days; even a conservative central bank like the SNB reversing 15 years of policy can ignite global fear and a one-way market fall with no recovery.
- **Verbatim quote:** "some news has come, you know, Switzerland has hiked interest rates. - **Source video:** #0186 — "186 - How People Lost HUGE Money by ignoring this SIMPLE Indication!.docx" (29 November 2020)
- **What happened:** Lakshmi Vilas Bank had been in trouble; its AGM was held the previous month with directors under scrutiny. On the evening of 17 November 2020, around 6 PM, the RBI announced that Lakshmi Vilas Bank equity would be completely written off, that the Development Bank of Singapore would take over the bank, and that the shares would be delisted. Despite this clear announcement, the NSE continued to allow trading of the stock from 17 November to 25 November 2020. On the first trading day after the announcement the price fell 20% (lower circuit), yet volume surged from ~3-7 lakh shares to 25 lakh shares. The next day it fell another 20% with 23 lakh shares traded. After two days at 20% lower circuit, the circuit was revised to 10%: the stock fell from 10 to 9 rupees and kept falling 10-20% daily while huge volumes continued -- turnovers reaching crores. On 24 November the company announced it was filing a case against RBI; the next day the price ticked up slightly and 31 crore rupees worth of shares traded (volume shot up to 4 crore shares, up 15-20%). On 25 November it was the last day of trading, then the stock was delisted. Many investors lost everything, calling the speaker asking what to do since the share value was zero.
- **Market impact:** Hundreds of crore rupees in trading turnover during the doomed rally; retail investors lost their entire investment as shares went to zero after delisting. Massive volume spikes (3 lakh to 25 lakh to 23 lakh to 12 lakh to 4 crore shares) showed uninformed buyers piling in after each 10-20% drop, treating the collapsing stock as attractive, until the final day of trading when it was delisted.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** When you know there is a problem or scam, keep away from those shares. Do your own research -- do not blindly buy just because a stock has fallen 20-30%. If RBI says equity is written off and the stock will be delisted, the price goes to zero. Nobody else will safeguard your money. Always follow news articles and make informed decisions.
- **Verbatim quote:** "So many people started calling me sir the price came down so much I thought it's a good buy and I thought if they win the case against RBI and the price will go up so now the shares are not trading sir so what should I do you cannot do anything the share value is zero and you have lost everything."

### Janet Yellen's Call for Coronavirus Relief Measures Triggers Global Market Rally — 18 January 2021
- **Source video:** #0233 — "233 - V-Shape Recovery - Another Attack Against Bears | Post Market Report 19-Jan-21" (19 January 2021)
- **What happened:** Janet Yellen, former Federal Reserve Chairman and newly confirmed Treasury Secretary in the Biden administration, stated that the US government should come out with more relief measures for coronavirus. This announcement came on the night of January 18, 2021 (reported on Jan 19 Post Market Report). The news triggered a massive short covering rally across global markets. Asian markets surged — Hong Kong's market was up 900 points at one point. Indian markets gap up more than 100 points and moved continuously higher throughout the day.
- **Market impact:** Nifty futures shot up nearly 350 points from the previous day's close to that day's high. The intraday action on Jan 18 saw Nifty fall 50 points at 1:30 PM, then reverse sharply up 150 points to 14,425, before falling again 175 points to close around 14,250. On Jan 19, the market opened with a gap up of 100+ points and continued climbing, described as a 'V-shaped recovery'. India VIX fell 6%. PR Sundar dubbed the candle the 'Janet Yellen candle' — comparable to the famous 'Nirmala candle'.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Market sentiment can flip rapidly on macro news. Short sellers who were active on bad news became weak when good news arrived. A speculator must watch the 'border' 24 hours and adjust positions as factors change — what was valid one or two days before may not hold. He managed the situation by selling 14,700 call options before the rally (limited loss of only 10 rupees despite Nifty rising 300+ points) and compensating with short put options (14,000 put sold at 15 rupees, closed below 5).
- **Verbatim quote:** "Yesterday night, Janet Ellen who was the Fed Chairman earlier, now is the Treasury Secretary in the new regime. And she said for coronavirus, the government should come out with more relief measures. Then what happened? Now the short sellers become less, the people are going long, they become more. That means the bulls are more. Now the bulls are chasing the bears."

### Global market sell-off and Indian market panic — January 2021 — January 25-27, 2021
- **Source video:** #0241 — "241 - PANIC in Stock Market Due To Global Sell-Off _ Post Market Repor.docx" (2021-01-27)

Bank Nifty fell ~3,000 points. Reliance Industries fell 10% in two days despite good results; L&T and IT stocks also fell despite excellent results — illustrating the 'buy on rumour, sell on news' and 'good news ignored in falling market' dynamics.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** In a falling market, all good news is ignored; in a rising market, all bad news is ignored. When everything looks bearish, the market may be near a bottom. The market was likely 'crying for chocolate' from the Fed — selling off to signal that not all is well and to elicit dovish stimulus. He also warns that FIIs were targeting FII counters (HDFC Bank, HDFC, Reliance) specifically.

- **What happened:** In just four trading sessions (with one public holiday — Republic Day on 26 January), Nifty fell from an opening level around 14,500 on Monday to break below 13,600 by Friday's close — a drop exceeding 900 points. Market participants widely attributed the crash to the GameStop short squeeze contagion spreading from US markets. The rapid, heavy fall across the week caught many by surprise.
- **Market impact:** The Indian equity market experienced a sharp, rapid correction of over 900 Nifty points in a single week. The crash was part of a broader global selloff. PR Sundar notes the fall was so fast that 'everything has gone very bad and everybody is puzzled why the markets are falling all over the world.' Despite the crash, he maintained that India remained in a firm bull market where 10-20% corrections are normal.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Corrections of 10-20% are frequent and normal in a bull market, and up to 30% is quite normal. For long-term investors, such downturns represent the right time to pick good stocks. He cautioned short-term traders about the volatility while urging long-term investors to stay the course. He also highlighted upcoming economic data (GST collection, PMI, auto sales, cement sales, core sector growth, US jobs data) that would add to volatility.
- **Verbatim quote:** "Just imagine on Monday morning, Nifty opened around 14,500. On Friday, around the closing time, it tested a low of, it even broke 13,600, which is a 900 point crash and that too with one public holiday, there are only four trading sessions. Four trading sessions, Monday morning high to Friday low, it was more than 900 points."

### NIFTY Surpasses 15,000 Milestone — 5 February 2021
- **Source video:** #0249 — "249 - NIFTY at 15K, SBI Candle, FII Impact... Post Market Report 05-02-2021" (2021-02-05)
- **What happened:** On 5 February 2021, the NIFTY 50 index crossed the 15,000 level for the first time. PR Sundar notes this was a dramatic rally: less than one year earlier (around 23 March 2020), NIFTY had crashed to approximately 7,500 during the COVID-19 market panic. The index had roughly doubled from that low in under a year. Sundar had previously published two videos predicting 15,000 would be reached quickly. The market opened consolidating but then formed an SBA candle with a 10% upper circuit within minutes, shocking skeptics who had expected a fall. Bank Nifty futures were trading at a significant discount to spot; when the freeze lifted, Bank Nifty surged 1,300 points from the previous close to the day's high before profit-booking erased over 1,000 points intraday.
- **Market impact:** NIFTY doubled from its COVID crash low of ~7,500 to 15,000 in less than a year — a major bull market rally. Crossing 15,000 represented a significant psychological and technical milestone for the Indian equity market, validating the thesis that resolving problems one by one drives markets higher.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Bull markets climb the wall of worries — as long as problems exist and are being solved one by one, markets move higher. When there are no problems left, that is the time to book profits and markets will fall. Stock markets work completely differently from conventional logic.
- **Verbatim quote:** "It is just less than an year and Nifty hit 7,500 late March, I think it's 23rd March or something like that and now it is less than one year from 7,500 to 15,000... bull market will climb the wall of worries. As long as there are problems, one by one problems are being solved, the markets will be moving higher, when there are no problems that is the time to book the profit and the markets will come down."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### 2019 Indian general election market episode (exit polls to results) — April-May 2019 (exit polls May 19, results May 23, 2019)

On actual result day, May 23, 2019, the market opened higher but closed well below the exit-poll day's high/close, then consolidated for ~1-1.5 weeks.

- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Historical election-year patterns repeat: a gap-up on favorable exit polls followed by a fade on actual results; do not chase and use the peak to hedge.

### Indian Equity Market Crash - FII Record Sell-Off (26 February 2021) — 26 February 2021
- **Source video:** #0272 — "272 - Dalal Street Week Ahead: MARCH 1st Week | 2021 | P R Sundar" (28 February 2021)
- **What happened:** On Friday 26 February 2021, Indian equity markets crashed dramatically. Nifty fell more than 700 points intra-day and Bank Nifty collapsed over 2000 points (approximately 5%). The rupee depreciated in the morning, signaling massive foreign institutional investor (FII) selling. FIIs were net sellers of 8,300 crore rupees; factoring in 5,000 crore of forced buying due to MSA (MSCI) rebalancing, the actual gross FII sell was estimated at over 13,000 crore — possibly the highest sell figure in Indian stock market history, exceeding even COVID-19 or Lehman Brothers collapse levels. Top banks including HDFC Bank, Kotak Bank, ICICI Bank, and State Bank of India all fell more than 5%. The India VIX spiked close to 30, a dangerously high zone, before partially recovering.
- **Market impact:** Nifty lost 700+ points; Bank Nifty fell 2000+ points (5%); all major bank stocks fell 5%+; VIX spiked to near 30; FII gross sell exceeded 13,000 crore — potentially the highest ever in Indian market history.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** After a severe market fall, recovery cannot be immediate — like a hospitalized patient who must rest and undergo treatment before getting back on their feet. Markets typically bottom out near the 50-day moving average (14,400-14,450 for Nifty at the time). Option writers can benefit in such volatile periods with high premiums, but markets can be unpredictable — Bank Nifty falling 2000 points in one day illustrates the 'magic of higher weeks'. Technical indicators like open interest are guidelines, not golden rules; PR Sundar personally traded a put ratio spread (bought 14,600 PE, sold double quantity of 14,000 PE).
- **Verbatim quote:** "Until Thursday everything was okay but on Friday the markets fell so much. At some point Nifty has fallen more than 700 points and Bank Nifty fell more than 2000 points. It was really a shocking."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### Global Bitcoin Crash and India COVID-19 Perfect Storm — April 19, 2021 — 19 April 2021
- **Source video:** #0322 — "322 - MONDAY MAYHEM! Post Market Report 19-04-2021.docx" (19 April 2021, 06:28:45 PM)
- **What happened:** April 19, 2021 was a 'perfect storm' market day combining multiple negative catalysts: (1) the escalating India COVID-19 crisis — Sundar described horrific scenes including black-market remdesivir selling at 25,000-50,000 rupees, hospital beds at 5 lakh rupees/day, a central minister's brother affected, and ambulance queues with dead bodies; (2) HDFC Bank results expected below expectations; (3) a global Bitcoin crash that Sundar worried would trigger cross-asset selling as losers liquidate other assets to cover losses; (4) FII selling of 1,633 crores on the first sign of trouble. Nifty fell more than 400 points, breaking the previous 14,250-14,260 support level to a low of 14,213. Bank Nifty dropped over 1,500 points intraday before recovering 900 points.
- **Market impact:** Nifty broke its previous support at 14,250-14,260 to an intraday low of 14,213 — the lowest level in a sequence of April corrections following February's 15,000 expiry. FIIs sold 1,633 crores while DIIs pumped in 2,355 crores. Options sellers were forced to shut the market to hedge, which accelerated the downside. Everything fell except IT stocks (Infosys/Wipro 'India weeks') which were up over 10%.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** In a 'perfect storm' where multiple adverse events converge — pandemic horror news + weak corporate results + crypto crash contagion + FII panic selling — traditional technical analysis (open interest, support levels) breaks down because options sellers mechanically hedge by selling into the decline. ### WTI Crude Oil Futures Trade Negative ($37/barrel) — April 2020 — 20 April 2020
- **Source video:** #0041 — "41 - How CRUDE OIL Prices Fell Below $0 _ P R Sundar.docx" (21 April 2020)
- **What happened:** On April 20, 2020 (the day before the video), WTI crude oil futures for the expiring April 2020 contract traded at minus $37 per barrel — the first time in history oil prices went negative. Traders holding the contract faced physical delivery obligations but discovered that most oil storage facilities were completely full, making storage impossible. This triggered panic selling at any price, driving the contract into negative territory. The June 2020 contracts remained unaffected and were trading normally.
- **Market impact:** For the first time in history, crude oil prices fell below zero. The expiring April 2020 WTI contract collapsed to -$37.63/bbl. The event exposed the fragility of commodity futures markets when physical delivery logistics break down during a supply glut. It became the defining market event of the COVID-19 volatility period and a textbook example of a black swan in commodity markets.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Never enter a commodity futures trade without fully understanding the delivery mechanics and storage realities. Buyers who thought they could simply take delivery and store the oil were blindsided — they ended up paying to get rid of a product they couldn't store. Also, don't confuse the expiring front-month contract (which can go to extremes) with the forward curve (June contracts were fine).
- **Verbatim quote:** "The shocking news came, most of the storage facilities are completely full. So, no more storage is possible. And that has created a huge panic among the buyers. So, they were ready to sell at any price. So, that is why the crude oil has come to trade in negative territory."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

- **What happened:** In 2004, then Finance Minister P. STT applied on every transaction regardless of whether the trader made a profit or a loss, and was later made non-deductible from final tax liability.
- **Market impact:** STT became a recurring burden because, as PR Sundar notes, more than 95% of market participants make losses yet still pay the tax on every trade. The rate for option traders was later raised from 0.1% to 0.5% (a fivefold increase) even though ~90% of Indian market volume is in options, creating what he calls a double-taxation problem after LTCG was reintroduced under the BJP government.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Double taxation is unfair — STT should be abolished now that LTCG is reintroduced, or at minimum made tax-deductible. He jokes it should be renamed a 'security transaction punishment' rather than a tax, and urges the Finance Minister to reduce STT on option selling to parity with futures.
- **Verbatim quote:** "I think in 2004, the then finance minister, P. Chidambaram, there was a demand to abolish the long-term capital gain tax. So, he abolished the long-term capital gain tax. So, that time he said... collecting the tax at the source is always an efficient way. So, he then introduced this securities transaction tax in lieu of long-term capital gain tax."

- **Source video:** #0253 — "253 - Dalal Street Week Ahead: FEB 2021 Week 2 - Budget Impact, Sizevi.docx" (09 February 2021)

This massive erroneous sell order triggered panic selling. By the time NSE realized the market had fallen 10% (which should have triggered circuit breakers), it had already fallen another 5%. - **Market impact:** A 15% one-minute fall in Nifty — far exceeding the 10% circuit breaker threshold. The market crashed dramatically within a minute before the exchange could react. The erroneous trade was reversed and the market closed nearly flat, but the episode exposed how a single fat-finger error could nearly bring down the index before circuit breakers could engage.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Although modern checks and balances now make such errors less likely, violent market moves (Nifty moving more than 3%) can still happen, and peak margin penalties should be waived in such scenarios — just as exchange penalties are already waived when Nifty makes a >3% move. Regulatory authorities should examine whether the same waiver logic should apply to peak margin rules.

### MK Global error trade — Nifty crashes 15% in minutes (2011) — 2011
- **Source video:** #0051 — "51 - Why Technical Analysis WORKS in India _ P R Sundar.docx" (29 April 2020)
- **What happened:** In 2011, the Nifty index fell approximately 15% within a few minutes. The Nifty futures, however, only fell 3-4%, creating a massive premium/discrepancy. The NSE was completely unprepared — their circuit breaker system is designed to halt trading at a 10% fall, but by the time they realized the market had hit 10%, it had already fallen to 15%. NSE activated its surveillance system and discovered the cause: a broker called MK Global Financial Services had made an error trade. A dealer was asked to sell shares worth 50 lakh rupees (one basket of Nifty), but misinterpreted the instruction and sold 50 lakh baskets instead — effectively selling 50 lakh × 50 lakh = 50,000 crore worth of shares. This massive erroneous sell order crashed the market.
- **Market impact:** The market crashed 15% in minutes. NSE identified the error, called MK Global, and directed them to buy back all the shares they sold since they had no delivery. MK Global panicked and bought back the entire quantity, which then shot the market back up 15%. Technical analysts who had gone short on the falling market had their stop losses triggered in both directions — first on the crash, then on the reversal.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** This is a second example where technical analysis trapped traders. The market fell 15% with no fundamental reason — it was a single broker's error trade. Technical analysts shorting the falling chart got stopped out. You must consider all factors, not just chart patterns.
- **Verbatim quote:** "In 2011, Nifty fell 15% within few minutes. But if you look carefully, Nifty is falling 15%, but the Nifty future fell only 3 or 4%. So, why Nifty when it is falling 15%? The Nifty future is falling only 3-4%. How come Nifty future trading at 10-12% premium? That is one question. Second question, how can a market fall 15% without any reason? Even the NSE was so surprised because they were not prepared. 10% down, they are supposed to close the exchange. But by the time they realized it has fallen 10%, it has already gone 15%."

He also draws a parallel to advising the NSC (Naval Staff College) that the previous day's market move was just an aberration and that markets are likely to recover — reflecting his broader lesson that extreme intraday moves can be technical glitches rather than fundamental shifts, and that recovery can follow quickly.

### India-Mauritius DTAA amendment makes post-2017 FPI investments taxable (2017) — 2017
- **Source video:** #2214 — "2214 - Mauritius TAX Issue Can Ruin INDIAN Markets More Than You Think!.docx" ()
- **What happened:** India renegotiated its Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement with Mauritius so that foreign portfolio investors investing in India after 2017 became liable to pay capital gains tax to India. Investments made before 2017 were grandfathered (exempt). Mauritius had no capital gains tax, so routing money through a Mauritius entity had previously allowed FPIs to avoid Indian capital gains tax entirely.
- **Market impact:** Speaker says it 'has been going on well' afterwards with investors paying tax; no specific crash attributed to this event itself, but it laid the groundwork for later FPI tax disputes.

- **Source video:** #0051 — "51 - Why Technical Analysis WORKS in India _ P R Sundar.docx" (29 April 2020)
- **What happened:** On May 31, 2018, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced that Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) could increase their shareholding in HDFC Bank beyond the existing FII limit. Technical analysts who went long on the cash market chart (seeing rising price and high buy volume) had their stop losses triggered and lost heavily. Those who understood the RBI FII window mechanics could arbitrage: buy in cash at a premium, short an equivalent quantity in futures, then square the futures profit when the price fell.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Technical analysis alone is insufficient — you must understand the underlying event drivers. A pure technical analyst watching HDFC Bank's rising chart would have gone long and lost money, while someone who understood the FII window mechanics could profit. Always look at everything, not just charts.

### US Stimulus Negotiations Collapse — Pelosi's Tuesday Deadline Passes With No Deal, Triggering Global Market Selloff — 2020-10-20
- **Source video:** #0175 — "175 - Impact of BINARY EVENT | Post Market Report | 21 Oct 2020.docx" (2020-10-21)
- **What happened:** House Speaker Nancy Pelosi had set a deadline that any US stimulus package must be agreed by Tuesday (October 20, 2020), otherwise it would not happen until after the election. At Tuesday midnight, no agreement had been reached — negotiations were still ongoing with no news. The failure to pass stimulus by the deadline triggered a global market reaction. In India, profit booking set in severely: Bank Nifty fell almost 750 points and Nifty fell almost 250 points. European markets had also fallen on coronavirus resurgence concerns, compounding the selloff.
- **Market impact:** Severe profit booking in Indian markets: Bank Nifty fell ~750 points, Nifty fell ~250 points. The market fell after 12:30 when European markets opened and then recovered ~80% of losses by end of day in a dramatic recovery. Nifty had crossed 12,000 earlier in the day before the fall. FIIs bought ₹2,100 crores while DIIs sold ₹1,600 crores.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Binary events (two possible outcomes) create uncertainty and increase volatility, which increases option premiums. When a binary event like US stimulus fails to produce news, markets react with sharp profit booking. The VIX (Wix) rises in such environments — it measures two-way movement possibility, not just downside fear. Rising markets can still see rising VIX. Traders should expect stop losses to be hit on both sides during binary event volatility.
- **Verbatim quote:** "Yesterday, the house speaker, Nancy Pelosi, a few days before she said, if at all US stimulus has to happen, it must happen by Tuesday. Otherwise, it is not going to happen until after the election. So, the whole world was watching, will there be stimulus or not? Either there can be agreement between Republicans and Democrats, there will be a stimulus or there is no agreement, no stimulus."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### RBI COVID-19 Loan Moratorium & Supreme Court Interest Waiver Case — March 2020 – September 2020
- **Source video:** #0150 — "150 - Loan Moratorium Supreme Court Case - 3 Possibilities!" (04 September 2020)
- **What happened:** Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a loan repayment moratorium in March 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic, initially for 3 months, later extended by another 3 months (total 6 months). Borrowers were allowed to defer EMI payments. However, unpaid amounts were added to principal and interest continued to accrue. Borrowers petitioned the Supreme Court seeking a waiver of interest during the moratorium period, arguing it was an act of God and businesses could not operate. Banks countered that they must pay interest to depositors (at ~5%) and therefore must collect interest from borrowers (at ~8%), otherwise their net interest income (the ~3% spread) would be wiped out. The central government formally declined to pay the interest on behalf of borrowers. Three possibilities were being debated in the Supreme Court: (1) government pays the interest to banks, (2) borrowers must pay full interest, (3) borrowers pay reduced interest (e.g., only the 5% cost to banks, not the full 8% profit margin).
- **Market impact:** Bank Nifty fell more than 2000 points in one week (Monday high to Friday slow). Banking stocks were hugely underperforming. The market was described as 'too much worried about the outcome of this case.' Indian markets failed to rise when US markets rose but fell when US markets fell, indicating particular weakness in the banking sector. Clarity on the Supreme Court case outcome was seen as necessary for market recovery.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Regulatory and legal uncertainty around policy decisions (like loan moratoriums and interest waivers) can cause significant sector-specific market weakness. Banking stocks are particularly sensitive to such policy outcomes because their business model depends on the net interest margin. Markets need clarity on regulatory case outcomes before recovering.
- **Verbatim quote:** "Because of coronavirus, the businesses were not doing well and the people who have taken a loan, the Reserve Bank of India said that you don't have to repay the loan for a few months, for three months. That is called moratorium. Moratorium means you don't have to pay the EMI. First three months moratorium was given, after that the three more months was given extra. So, a total of six months period, the people who have taken loan, they were allowed not to pay the EMI."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

Approximately 30,000 crore rupees was invested in these debt mutual funds.
- **Market impact:** Ultra-HNI clients had invested their collateral capital in Franklin Templeton debt funds and given those funds as collateral to the exchange to obtain trading limits for options/futures positions. When Franklin Templeton wound up the schemes, the exchange set the collateral value of these six mutual funds to zero because the collateral could no longer be encashed if a client defaulted. This forced all option sellers and futures players who had used these funds as collateral to immediately close their positions since they lost their collateral-based limits. This forced liquidation created an imbalance in the demand and supply scenario, which was the main reason the markets fell on that Friday.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** The butterfly effect from chaos theory applies to markets: what happens on a small scale in one place affects the system on a big scale elsewhere. Whatever happens anywhere in the world, the first thing to be affected will be the stock market. Option sellers' reliance on debt mutual funds as collateral creates a hidden linkage between mutual fund crises and equity market volatility.

### NSE Technical Glitch and Communication Breakdown (24 February 2021) — 2021-02-24
- **Source video:** #0268 — "268 - Stock Market's Highest Form of Gambling? (S01E01).docx" (2021-02-24)
- **What happened:** On 24 February 2021, around 10:08 AM, NSE trading was proceeding normally with prices refreshing but the index not refreshing. NSE decided to stop trading. Initially, news indicated trading would be suspended at 11:40 for both cash and F&O segments, but only F&O was halted at 11:40; the cash market continued until 11:43. NSE cited a problem with the communication network and said it would take time to resolve. Multiple conflicting announcements followed: at 13:00 news came that the pre-open session would start, then at 14:50 that the market would start, and later this was unconfirmed — indicating the issue was not resolved. The lack of clear, consistent communication caused widespread uncertainty, with speculation about whether trading would be extended beyond the normal 3:30 PM close.
- **Market impact:** Brokers became scared because market participants had already taken intraday positions that needed to be squared up before the 3:30 PM close. The uncertainty about whether trading would resume and for how long created significant stress and speculation in the market. The incident highlighted that the communication failure was arguably more serious than the technical glitch itself.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** The more serious problem than a technical glitch is the communication surrounding it. NSE should have proactively informed brokers as soon as the glitch was resolved that trading would continue for at least one to one-and-a-half hours after 3:30 PM. Clear, timely communication is essential during exchange disruptions to prevent panic and uncertainty among brokers and traders.
- **Verbatim quote:** "You know this kind of thing can happen, technical glitch can happen but what is more serious than the glitch? The more serious problem than the technical glitch is the communication. Nobody knew what is going to happen... they have not resolved the issue and many people started speculating what is going to happen, will the trading be extended."

Interest rate increases from near-zero levels (0 to 0.25% or 0.25 to 0.5%) are unlikely to cause mass share disposal. The 2003-2007 Indian bull run occurred while interest rates kept rising — what matters is whether the economy grows faster than rates. Market corrections in a bull run are 'fast and furious' but shallow; the current pullback is normal profit booking, not a trend reversal.

### Bank Nifty 37100 Put Freak Trade / 920-Straddle Manipulation — 2021-09-03
- **Source video:** #0562 — "562 - Reliance Pushes Nifty All Time High _ Post Market Report 03-Sep-21.docx" ()
- **What happened:** At 10:29:58 the Bank Nifty 37100 put option traded around 358-360 rupees; one second later (10:29:59) it spiked to 1921.80 rupees with 252,000 contracts traded in that single second. PR Sundar describes it as a manipulator-driven freak trade targeting retail traders who ran the popular '920 straddle' (selling ATM call and put at 9:20 AM with stop-loss market orders on both sides). Manipulators who had shorted Bank Nifty/HDFC Bank pocketed roughly 38 crore in one second while stop-loss-market-order sellers lost ~38 crore.
- **Market impact:** Wiped out a broad group of retail options traders running the crowded 920 straddle; about 38 crore was transferred from stop-loss sellers to the manipulators in a single second. Sparked widespread panic and triggered PR Sundar's warning against stop-loss market orders.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Never place a stop-loss market order (use a wide-range stop-loss limit instead), and never blindly follow crowded strategies because manipulators deliberately target them. Modify any learned system to suit your own risk profile.
- **Verbatim quote:** "today at 1029.58 this 37100 put option was trading around 358, 360 rupees, just one second later 1029.59 just one second in that one second that 360 rupees shot up to 1921 rupees 80 pies, can you imagine how many contracts traded, 252000 quantity has been traded in that one second"

Domestic institutions with strong capital buffers (mutual fund flows) typically absorb such shocks and buy at lower levels, often leading to recovery and new highs.

### Exchanges/SEBI remove the 'Do Not Exercise' option for in-the-money option buyers — November 2021
- **Source video:** #0785 — "785 - MARGIN FOR OPTION BUYERS! No More _Do Not Exercise_ Option!.docx" ()
- **What happened:** PR Sundar explains that the exchange previously allowed in-the-money option buyers (within the at-the-money strike plus three strikes down) to elect a 'do not exercise' option to avoid physical delivery. Under that provision, a buyer could walk away and forfeit the intrinsic value rather than take/give delivery. From November 2021 this provision was removed, so there is no longer any such escape route available in the market.
- **Market impact:** Option buyers who are near the money can no longer avoid compulsory physical delivery through the 'do not exercise' route; they must square off or face delivery and the associated risk of large/unlimited losses. Retail option buyers lost a protective workaround.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Don't trade stock options; if you do, square off at least a day before expiry; and if an option goes in-the-money on expiry day with no liquidity, take a counter position in futures to avoid physical delivery.
- **Verbatim quote:** "earlier exchange had this provision at the money strike plus three strike prices within that range if your option is in the money you don't want to exercise you don't want to give physical delivery you can leave it but you will not get even one rupee you will lose all the money... what has happened in the last november they have removed it so there is no such option was available since november 2021"

### NSE directs brokers to refund peak margin penalties wrongly charged to clients (Sept 2, 2022 circular) — 2022-09-02
- **Source video:** #1252 — "1252 - CLAIM YOUR REFUND! NSE Slams Brokers for Margin Penalty SCAM!.docx" ()
- **What happened:** SEBI introduced the peak margin penalty framework under which any penalty for short/non-collection of upfront margin must be paid by the broker (member) to the clearing corporation/exchange, NOT by the client. Exchanges had already clarified this via NSE circular dated July 31, 2020 and reiterated it via a circular dated October 12, 2021. Despite these clarifications, almost all brokers across the industry began deducting peak margin penalty (lakhs of rupees in some cases) directly from client accounts. PR Sundar and others filed an RTI with SEBI, which confirmed no such penalty can be levied on clients. On September 2, 2022 (NSE circular ref 602022), NSE again reiterated that members are not permitted to pass on such penalties to clients under any circumstances and directed brokers to refund any penalties passed on to clients after November 11, 2021, on an immediate basis.
- **Market impact:** Widespread, industry-wide deduction of peak margin penalty from retail client accounts (reported in lakhs) is unlawful; affected clients are entitled to full refunds. Brokers argue the mandatory penalty burden on them (in a low-margin, highly competitive industry) is unfair and some are reportedly collecting higher margins than mandated to avoid the penalty.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Clients should check their ledger statements; if any peak margin penalty was charged, demand a full refund citing the NSE Sept 2, 2022 circular, since brokers had no right to deduct it at all (it should be zero). He also warns brokers may be over-collecting margin (one unconfirmed report of a top broker adding 3%) and urges exchanges/SEBI/brokers to find a fair solution.
- **Verbatim quote:** "However, exchange has observed that certain members are passing on the penalty levied by clearing corporation on account of short non collection of upfront margin from clients to respective clients. In view of the above, it is once again reiterated that members are not permitted to pass on the penalty levied by the clearing corporation on account of short non collection of upfront margin to clients under any circumstances. Further, members are advised to refund the penalty levied by the clearing corporations on account of short non collection of upfront margins to the clients on an immediate basis if same has been passed on to the clients after 11th October, 2021."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### Bank of Japan raises interest rates on July 31, 2024, triggering yen carry-trade unwind — 2024-07-31
- **Source video:** #2281 — "2281 - Pre Market Report 05-Aug-2024.txt" ()
- **What happened:** On July 31, 2024, the Bank of Japan increased its interest rate, ending the long-standing near-zero rate regime. With Japanese rates at zero, traders had borrowed yen cheaply to invest in higher-yielding markets (the yen carry trade). The rate hike caused the yen to appreciate; although borrowers paid no interest, the capital appreciation of the yen created losses for those who had borrowed in yen and invested in other currencies, forcing a violent unwinding of carry trades.
- **Market impact:** The appreciating yen and forced carry-trade unwind contributed to a sharp global sell-off across equity markets, including Japanese and US markets, and pressured Indian markets as well.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** PR Sundar explains the yen carry-trade mechanism as one of the three main triggers of the global crash, showing how a Japanese policy move ripples worldwide through leveraged cross-currency trades.
- **Verbatim quote:** "In Japan markets, when the interest rates are zero, people borrow money and then invest in other markets. Now, on July 31st, Japan has increased the interest rate. So, therefore, Japanese yen is appreciating. Although you don't pay interest to the Japan, but capital appreciation in Japanese yen will make a dent for the people who borrow from yen and trade in other currencies."

- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Never borrow capital to trade or invest; you cannot fight the government/regulator — if policy aims to shrink volumes, comply, because regulators can always tighten further (e.g., raise the extreme loss margin from 2% to 5-10%). His broader takeaway: stop intraday trading in Indian exchanges; the rules are designed to kill the segment.

- **Source video:** #2748 — "2748 - JANE STREET Spoiled Dalal Street.txt" ()
- **What happened:** PR Sundar recounts that SEBI issued a ruling against the US trading firm Jane Street for manipulating the Indian index options market. He alleges Jane Street built positions of about ₹45,000 crore in index options and ₹5,000 crore in index futures, dumped large sell orders in a single second to trigger index free-falls, and bought large volumes of put options to profit when the index was driven down. He claims option prices—not the underlying—were dictating the index, with put premiums rising even as markets rose, distorting the market for over a year. In response, SEBI levied a penalty of about ₹5,000 crore and barred Jane Street from trading in Indian markets.
- **Market impact:** According to PR Sundar, the manipulation made it extremely difficult for Indian retail and proprietary traders to make money for over a year, producing abnormal gap-ups/gap-downs and distorted option pricing. He describes Jane Street as having 'spoiled Dalal Street' and says the full impact of the manipulation is still not fully known.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** PR Sundar argues regulators must protect genuine lower-risk participants (e.g., covered-call sellers holding shares in their demat account) rather than penalising them, and should instead cap per-entity gross F&O exposure (e.g., break large orders into ₹100 crore chunks per minute) to stop manipulators. He contends SEBI's rules inadvertently restricted legitimate hedgers while a foreign firm bypassed position limits.
- **Verbatim quote:** "We all know now that Sebi has come out with ruling against Jane Street. So about 5,000 crore penalty. They are not allowed to trade in Indian markets and all these are okay."

### 2026 Union Budget STT hike hits derivatives and cash market — February 2026 (Union Budget)
- **Source video:** #3035 — "3035 - Year 26, NIFTY 26K-.txt" ()
- **What happened:** In the 2026 budget the Securities Transaction Tax (STT) was increased rather than reduced or removed, contrary to widespread expectations of relief (cut/removal of STT, lower LTCG tax, new LTCG slab). Sundar states STT on option selling has been raised seven to eight times over the BJP government's tenure, and this budget raised futures STT by 1.5x (a 150% increase).
- **Market impact:** The market fell after the budget because none of the expected reliefs materialized and taxes were instead raised; this also pushed Nifty temporarily below 25,000 on budget day. F&O sentiment, already weak from FII selling, worsened.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Budget tax policy is a direct market trigger; when expected relief is absent and taxes rise, sentiment and prices fall. The government is perceived as anti-stock-market, yet retail mutual-fund flows prop up the market.
- **Verbatim quote:** "On the contrary, in the budget, the STT was increased. That too, the increase in STT was so high that during the BJP government option spreading, STT has been increased seven to eight times. Even the futures also, STT this time, it is increased by one and a half times. 150 percent increase in the tax. So because of that, once again, the market fell."
- **Confidence:** medium | **Web verification:** not enriched

### Iran–Israel–US war and Strait of Hormuz closure send oil to ~$110 and trigger global market panic (March 2026) — March 2026 (around 07–09 Mar 2026)
- **Source video:** #3057 — "3057 - Pre Market Report 09-Mar-2026.txt" ()
- **What happened:** PR Sundar describes an escalating war between Iran, Israel and the US. Iran appeared to be losing the war but could still sustain and inflict damage on other markets. The Strait of Hormuz — through which India imports roughly 80% of its crude — was effectively shut, driving crude to about $110/barrel (he had predicted it would open above $100). Two days earlier, a report that Iran had agreed to talks had lifted Nifty futures ~400–500 points to nearly 25,000, but that reversed into a vertical ~1,200-point drop. Israel was reported to have bombed an oil storage tank in Tehran, adding fuel to the panic.
- **Market impact:** Global risk-off panic: South Korean market down ~6% in the morning, US and European futures down 2–3%, GIFT Nifty indicating ~3% gap down, Nifty futures fell ~1,200 points from ~25,000, Bank Nifty expected to fall another 2–3%; crude above $100/barrel.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** In violent, event-driven markets, hedging is mandatory, cut long positions, don't try to catch a falling market, and it is better to step away until things settle rather than suffer random losses. Asia (especially oil-importing India) is worst hit by such oil shocks.
- **Verbatim quote:** "this bark between Iran and Israel and Iran and the US, the worst affected people are not there, Israel are not the US, it is the Asian people. Why? Because we get around 80% of our oil through the Strait of Hormuz and which has been completely closed."
- **Confidence:** medium | **Web verification:** not enriched

### Iran-Israel missile conflict and Trump's 5-day postponement of a planned attack — March 2026 (around 24-Mar-26)
- **Source video:** #3078 — "3078 - MANIPULATED Markets- Post Market Report 24-Mar-26.txt" ()
- **What happened:** PR narrates an ongoing Iran-Israel conflict: per some reports Iran launched a number of missiles against Israel (unconfirmed; his Dubai contacts had not heard attacks/drones in 24 hours). Separately, Trump postponed a planned attack by 5 days, with that window ending toward the end of that weekend, creating recurring weekend uncertainty. He says the US market is subject to Trump's tweets and India is similarly whipsawed by such headline risk.
- **Market impact:** Crude oil prices rose, sparking inflation/interest-rate fears that hit banking stocks (HDFC Bank down ~25% in 3 months, contributing an estimated 750-800 Nifty points of drag). Nifty was extremely volatile, US futures and European markets whipsawed between positive and negative, and the 5-day Trump deadline plus weekend uncertainty kept the market on edge.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Geopolitical headline risk (Trump statements, Iran news) makes markets hostage to violent, unpredictable swings; verify before reacting, respect weekend uncertainty, and assume the worst may be over but 'we are not yet out of the woods.'
- **Verbatim quote:** "But you know like remember there is no ceasefire talk is just only Trump has postponed the attack by 5 days. So that 5 days will be ending towards the end of this weekend. Again the weekend uncertainty will be there. But don't worry Monday morning and definitely Trump will say something to move the market up or down as per their wish and next Monday."
- **Confidence:** medium | **Web verification:** not enriched

### Iran–US conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure drive crude oil spike and dent Indian market sentiment — April 2026 (ongoing around the recording week)
- **Source video:** #3098 — "3098 - Dalal Street Week Ahead- APRIL 4TH Week - 2026 - P R Sundar.txt" ()
- **What happened:** The speaker describes an unresolved Iran–US standoff in which the Strait of Hormuz (mis-transcribed as 'streets of Armas'/'streets of farmers') remains closed, ships are not sailing through, and crude oil jumped from about $95 per barrel to $107 (later easing to ~$104). Iran initially denied talks, then sent its Foreign Minister to Islamabad but stated it would not meet the US face-to-face; the US cancelled sending two negotiators to Pakistan. A ceasefire deadline had passed with no direct attack by either side, but the shipping closure persists.
- **Market impact:** The crude spike dented sentiment in India and compounded selling pressure; the speaker says any rally would be 'sold into' until crude falls below $100 and the Strait reopens. Together with IT stock weakness it triggered a Nifty free fall of ~400 points on Friday and an ~800-point drop from the week's high to low. Indian markets could only look for a rally once the Strait reopens and crude falls.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Until the geopolitical/commodity shock (Strait of Hormuz closure and elevated crude) resolves, rallies should be treated as sellable; the Indian market cannot sustain a rebound while crude stays high and shipping is disrupted.
- **Verbatim quote:** "the streets of Armas are still not resolved, the ships are not sailing through, the crew prices moving higher. You know, from around $95 per barrel is shot up to $107. So that is already dinting the sentiment in India and top of which this IT stocks under performance, you know, it is adding fuel to the fire or adding salt to the wood."
- **Confidence:** high | **Web verification:** not enriched

### US-Iran ceasefire collapses, Nifty drops 500+ points — July 2026 (early July, during July F&O series)
- **Source video:** #3221 — "3221 - Finally Markets BREAKING OUT- Post Market Report 31-Jul-26.txt" ()
- **What happened:** PR Sundar recounts that during the July F&O series, after four strong up-sessions, news broke that the ceasefire between the US and Iran had ended. The very next trading day the Nifty fell more than 500 points, erasing the gains of the first four sessions.
- **Market impact:** Nifty fell more than 500 points, wiping out the first four days of gains in the July series.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Geopolitical headline news can override technical signals; his technical long/short indicator gave 4-5 wrong signals in recent months largely because of geopolitical tension, so traders should not rely blindly on technicals and must manage risk.
- **Verbatim quote:** "the bad news came that there is no more ceasefire between US and Iran and then the very next day, the Nifty fell more than 500 points, so the wiping out the first four days of gain."
- **Confidence:** medium | **Web verification:** not enriched

### Trump's 'no ceasefire with Iran' announcement triggers July 2026 market fall — July 2026
- **Source video:** #3223 — "3223 - RALLY Continues- Post Market Report 03-Aug-26.txt" ()
- **What happened:** After the first five trading sessions of July 2026 had been performing extremely well, former US President Trump announced that there was no ceasefire with Iran. This headline caused a big fall in the Indian market, and for the rest of the month the market consolidated rather than continuing higher.
- **Market impact:** Caused a large sudden fall in the Indian market; the Nifty then consolidated for the remainder of July 2026 instead of continuing its early-month rally.
- **PR Sundar's lesson:** Geopolitical headline shocks cause sharp, discrete market moves, but markets eventually get 'used to' ongoing geopolitical tension (the Iran-US 'cat and mouse game'); Indian markets had largely adapted to it by early August.
- **Verbatim quote:** "And that is when this Trump announcement that there is no ceasefire with Iran, you know, made a big fall. And then for the rest of the month, we were consolidating."
- **Confidence:** medium | **Web verification:** not enriched
